verdict: Visa's net revenue rose 10% to $8.8B as cross-border volume jumped 16% — but a $430M litigation provision held GAAP profit growth to 10%, at $4.7B.

segments.name: Service revenue
segments.note: Fees based on the payments volume Visa's clients processed in the prior quarter, which rose 8% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Data processing revenue
segments.note: Fees for authorizing, clearing and settling each transaction on Visa's network; processed transactions rose 11%.

segments.name: International transaction revenue
segments.note: Fees when a card is used outside its home country — the cross-border business; cross-border volume rose 16% in constant dollars.

segments.name: Other revenue
segments.note: Value-added services, consulting and other fees.

opex.name: Personnel
opex.note: Salaries and benefits for the people who run the network.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — offices, legal and administration, including lease consolidation costs (see one-time items).

opex.name: Marketing
opex.note: Advertising and sponsorships that keep the Visa brand in front of cardholders.

opex.name: Litigation provision
opex.note: Setting money aside for legal cases (see one-time items).

opex.name: Network, professional & depreciation
opex.note: Running the network, outside professional help, and wear on Visa's technology — $189M network and processing, $160M professional fees and $249M depreciation and amortization.

otherDetail: Investment income and other income of $241M, partly offset by $82M of interest expense on Visa's debt.
follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Visa reports 'net revenue' of $8,775M; this page starts from gross revenue of $12,032M so the $3,257M of client incentives shows as a cost.

takeaways.title: Cross-border stayed hot
takeaways.text: Payments volume rose 8% in constant dollars and processed transactions 11%, while cross-border volume — the most lucrative traffic — jumped 16%, lifting international transaction revenue 9%.

takeaways.title: Every revenue line grew
takeaways.text: Net revenue rose 10% to $8,775M: service revenue +7%, data processing +12%, international transaction +9% and other revenue +37%, against client incentives of $3,257M paid back to card issuers.

takeaways.title: A legal provision held back GAAP profit
takeaways.text: Net income rose 10% to $4,663M and EPS 12% to $2.29 — held back by a $430M litigation provision. Excluding special items, non-GAAP EPS was $2.51, up 20%.

oneTimers: GAAP results include a $424M litigation provision for the interchange multidistrict litigation (MDL) injunctive relief class and other legal matters, plus $57M of lease consolidation costs. Excluding these and other special items, non-GAAP net income was $5,117M, or $2.51 per share.
